contract.goal: every module's operator controls on the /admin/v1/ surface under admin-authorization's model: identity and audit (access), reconciliation, file-ingest, outbox, job leases, messaging-db lag (stuck work), exports and file-actions (cross-requester), user-settings and PAT moved onto it; the reconciliation and fileingest actuator endpoints removed
contract.output: an ru.ludwigandreas.<module>.admin package + auto-configuration per area, Actor.tenant + audit_event.actor_tenant, OutboxStatus.DISCARDED, RunLock.forceRelease, removals with revapi.differences entries, grant blocks and regenerated OpenAPI documents in both services, README operation tables and admin-guide in both locales
constraints: follow the archived admin-authorization spec: no role names in starters, one gate, fail closed, reason on privileged, audit through AdminAudit in the service transaction
QueryDSL only (no new SQL outside the two carve-out packages)
no payload or content in any administrative response
new in-repo edges optional only (security starter, web starter) and acyclic as design section 2 checks
no POM change to ludwig-bom or ludwig-service-parent
known gate exceptions carried from admin-authorization: check_image_pins.sh false positive, check_api_baseline.sh unreachable repository

rollback_point: 44358a935e47d0353f0da2ec95f7baa04405f677 plus the uncommitted admin-authorization working-tree diff (archived as 2026-10-28-admin-authorization, not committed)
decisions: Task 2.2: forced release lives in a new RunLockAdministration (JDBC, short auto-commit connections, same style as JdbcRunLock), not on the RunLock interface as the task worded it. Every job holds a RunLock and must not be handed the power to break another job's lease; only the administrative endpoints use RunLockAdministration. JDBC rather than QueryDSL for the reason JdbcRunLock documents: a lease change must commit on its own connection, outside any caller transaction (run-lock spec).

Every area's auto-configuration lives in the module's config package, not in its admin package: job-core's first ArchitectureTest run reported spring.configuration-classes-reside-in-config-packages and persistence.persistence-context-is-confined (the auto-config touches DataSource) against ru.ludwigandreas.job.core.admin. Design section 1 updated.

rest-paths.controllers-declare-a-versioned-base-path required /api/v\d+ of every @RestController, which every administrative controller (under /admin/v1/ by spec) would violate in every module. Fixed at the root in architecture-rules: RestPathRules excludes classes declaring administrative handlers, whose path shape RuleGroup.ADMIN's mapped-under-the-versioned-prefix already owns - one owner per rule, per the enforcement triad. New AdminRulesTest case proves admin controllers are skipped and a non-administrative controller under /admin/ is still judged. Not done by widening each module's configured pattern.

A module running architecture tests over its admin package sets architecture.rules.conventions.types.base-exception = ru.ludwigandreas.webcore.problem.LocalizedException, as other modules do, so exceptions.custom-exceptions-extend-the-base-exception has its anchor.

job-core run-now answers 202 with the job view and dispatches via a new SelfSchedulingLifecycle.runSoon() (TaskScheduler.schedule(tick, now)), so the HTTP thread never runs the job; 409 when a lease of the job's name is held, or when the job is shutting down; forced release of an unheld lease is 409, of an unknown lease 404.

Adding the optional security edge to a module puts the security starter and web-core on that module's OWN test classpath, which broke outbox's 7 existing context tests in three layers, each fixed at its cause: (1) the security starter's fail-closed audience check - existing tests keep running exactly as before with `ludwig.security.enabled=false` in src/test/resources/application.properties (admin ITs turn it back on for themselves); (2) a latent web-core defect: WebCoreLocalizationAutoConfiguration.ValidationMessageConfiguration was conditional only on the jakarta.validation API but needs Hibernate Validator, so any context with the API and no provider failed with NoClassDefFoundError - fixed at the root by adding org.hibernate.validator.HibernateValidator to its @ConditionalOnClass (web-core is now a touched module; its dependents are in the gate anyway); (3) the API now present makes @Validated properties need a provider - spring-boot-starter-validation at test scope, the precedent file-action/export/pat already follow. Recipe for every remaining module gaining the edge (reconciliation, file-ingest, messaging-db, audit-spring-boot-starter).

Finding: the outbox module has no retention purge at all, so the outbox-admin spec's 'purged by the same retention as DEAD_LETTER' is vacuously true; discarded rows are kept. Not invented here; added to openspec/intents/admin-surface-follow-ups.md. The README states it.

Admin package shape for every area, forced by the shared rules on the outbox's first run (repositories-are-used-only-by-services, transactional-methods-are-in-the-service-layer, both keyed on package names): admin/<Area>AdminOperations, admin/service/{Service,Views,Exception}, admin/web/Controller, auto-config in config/, queries in repository/. The service owns its own filter record so the controller never imports from repository/. job-core was restructured to the same shape for consistency. Design section 1 updated.

Integration-test naming follows each module's actual binding, checked per module: job-core binds failsafe (so *IT runs); outbox binds none and runs its *IntegrationTest under surefire, so an *IT there would silently never run - OutboxAdminIT was renamed OutboxAdminIntegrationTest after confirming from the log that it had not executed.

Outbox admin changes lock the row first (QueryDSL PESSIMISTIC_WRITE; bulk retry with SKIP LOCKED): the dispatcher's native FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim bypasses the entity version, so load-then-save could overwrite a claim and discard a message already being sent. A refusal by state does not roll back (noRollbackFor), so the refused-by-state audit event survives.

messaging-db: per-partition positions are a new LogStore.positions() JDBC query beside the existing lag() (the module's documented JDBC store over a configurable schema), not a second data-access path. MessagingAdminIT builds a LogStore over the container and excludes MessagingDbAutoConfiguration so no listener containers start for a read endpoint.

Spec finding corrected: messaging-db-admin said a non-GET request is 'answered as an unmapped path'; Spring answers a wrong method on a mapped path with 405, which is the correct HTTP behaviour. Scenario now says 405 and no offset changes (code is the truth).

Reconciliation: ReconciliationAdminService is a faithful port of the deleted actuator endpoint's logic (same engine calls, same result maps), changed only at the edges: unknown task/enumeration/job/lease -> 404 LocalizedException with bundle codes (no English exception text reaches callers), destructive switch + confirm replaced by reconciliation.privileged + Admin-Reason, one AdminAudit record per action instead of a ReconciliationAuditEvent OPERATOR event. Category.OPERATOR removed (dead once the actuator went; revapi entry added to design section 9). Run/backfill are synchronous as before, so they answer 202 with a terminal SUCCEEDED envelope whose result link and Location are the task resource.

Spec gap fixed in reconciliation-admin: enumeration tasks had two task-level actuator actions the table omitted (discover, requeue-members); added as POST .../tasks/{task}/discover and .../members/requeue (operate) rather than dropping operator controls. EnumerationEndpointIntegrationTest was ported case by case to ReconciliationAdminIntegrationTest over MockMvc (15 cases, all passing first run), the destructive-switch cases becoming grant and reason cases.

spring-boot-actuator removed from reconciliation's POM (only the endpoint used it). ReconciliationArchitectureTest's package lists swapped ..reconciliation.actuator.. for ..reconciliation.admin.., so the admin package gets exactly the access the actuator had. Stale 'actuator' wording in javadoc and one log message reworded; changelog SQL comments left untouched because editing an applied changeset's text can change its checksum.

file-ingest: the actuator's run envelope marked a finished run SUCCEEDED with no result link, which OperationResponses rejects (the actuator never went through it, so this was latent). Its own javadoc had anticipated it: 'a link ... is the concrete thing a REST surface would add'. The run resource now exists and is the result link. The trigger returns the envelope rather than the entity, so the web layer never imports FileIngestRun. FileIngestProperties.Endpoint (enabled, recentRuns, allowManualRun) removed; recentRuns is now a constant 20 (its old default). SqlConfinementTest's api-must-not-see list swapped .actuator.. for .admin...

Audit: the actor-tenant changeset is 0005, not the 0003 the design and task named - 0001..0004 already exist and numbers are unique and ascending per module. Design and task text corrected. scripts/check_migrations.sh reads `git ls-files`, so the new untracked changeset was invisible to it (E_INCLUDE_MISSING); `git add -N` (intent-to-add, no content staged, nothing committed) made it visible, after which 101 changesets conform. Every new changeset in this change needs the same.

Audit trail search tenant rule reuses TenantScope exactly: USER with tenant T -> actor_tenant = T; USER without tenant -> actor_tenant IS NULL (everything, in a single-tenant service); SERVICE unconfined. In a multi-tenant service users always carry a tenant, so untenanted and pre-column rows are visible to services only, as the spec requires. The repository takes the scope as plain parameters, so the optional security types never reach the persistence layer.

Identity: spec said partner/grant changes record an event 'of category access'; AdminAudit, the one administrative audit path, writes category admin for every area. The single category is the design, so the spec scenario was corrected rather than special-casing one area (code is the truth). The README's 'Known gap' about these tables having no AuditEvent is removed in both locales: changes made through /admin/v1/identity/ are now audited in their transaction; changes made by hand in SQL still are not, which the README now says.

Identity: grants are read per request (DatabaseDataScopeProvider is uncached), so a grant or revocation takes effect at once on every replica; only partner changes evict, via ludwigAuthorityCache.evictAfterCommit(PrincipalRef.partner(code)). A grant's dimension is accepted only if the deployment has a DataScopeMapping for that resource supporting it (DataScopeRegistry); with no registry (data authorization off) a dimensioned grant is refused, since nothing could enforce it. Effective-authority inspection calls the raw AuthorityResolver, not the caching AuthorityLookup, and is audited. Grant listings for a confined (tenant) caller show only USER grants whose subject's projected tenant matches.

Identity test infrastructure, first real context in this module: it needs a JPAQueryFactory bean (a consuming-service concern its query repositories always had; supplied in the test application as crud-service-example's QuerydslConfig does), test-scoped test-support, test-support-security and spring-boot-starter-validation (layer 3 of the recipe), and projected users carry source_system as the Kafka mapper sets it.

Exports: the requester-scoped API let a caller holding ReportRunController.ADMIN_AUTHORITY = "ROLE_EXPORT_ADMIN" read, download and cancel anybody's run - a hard-coded role in a library, the exact thing this change removes, and contrary to export-admin's 'requester API keeps 404ing a non-requester'. Constant and branch removed (revapi entry added to design section 9); README row updated in both locales. Consequence stated plainly: no administrator can download another person's export output any more - the exports area shows runs without any output or result link, per the no-content rule.

Exports test: the shared ExportTestApplication deliberately excludes the security starter, so the admin IT has its own nested application (same sink bean, same rest-client/identity exclusions, security kept). Faster loop adopted from here on: `mvn -pl :<deps> -am install -DskipTests` once, then `mvn -pl :<module> verify`, which avoids both re-running every upstream module's tests and the stale-~/.m2 problem.

File-action: the admin cancel is FileActionService.cancelByAdministrator(id), not cancel(action, id): the requester cancel authorises against the action's required-authority and looks the submission up by action, neither of which applies to an administrator. Same store.requestCancellation and same file-action.cancellation-requested audit event, plus the admin event naming the submitter.
File-action listing filters on the envelope OperationStatus (`status=`, as the spec names it), mapped to the FileActionStates whose status() matches, rather than on FileActionState.
File-action admin rules run through the existing FileActionArchitectureTest (packages = ru.ludwigandreas.fileaction, which includes .admin); no separate AdminArchitectureTest.

Settings: SettingsAccessPolicy recognises an administrative caller by the bound AdminInvocation of the settings area (constructor takes Supplier<Optional<AdminInvocation>>, AdminInvocation::current in production, a fixed invocation in unit tests since bind is package-private). Another area's invocation is refused like any non-administrative caller. Cross-tenant inside a settings operation throws the new SettingsSubjectNotFoundException (404, code ludwig.user-settings.error.subject-not-found); outside, SettingsAccessDeniedException keeps 403.

Settings: the default SecurityContextTenantResolver gives every subject the caller's tenant, so the cross-tenant 404 is reachable only with a resolver that knows the subject's tenant; the settings-admin spec scenario was tightened to say so and SettingsAdminIntegrationTest supplies such a resolver. No subject-tenant lookup was invented.

Settings: controllers moved to ru.ludwigandreas.usersettings.admin.web under @RequestMapping("/admin/v1/settings"); their beans moved from UserSettingsWebAutoConfiguration to the new UserSettingsAdminAutoConfiguration (ConditionalOnBean AdminOperationCatalog + SettingsResponseRenderer + SettingsWriter, web.enabled, backfill-enabled kept on the backfill bean). The backfill controller's requireAdmin call was dropped: the guard requires settings.operate and the tenant is the caller's by construction.

Settings: the OwnerModeIntegrationTest 'administrator read is audited' case moved to SettingsAdminIntegrationTest, where it goes through the real guard; test-support-security added at test scope. README property rows for admin-authority/admin-base-path are left for 14.2.

PAT: PatAuthorities.MANAGE_ANY removed; the self-service controller acts only on the caller's own tokens (other owner: 403 via AccessDeniedException; on issue the attempt is first audited as pat.issuance-refused through the new PatService.recordIssuanceForAnotherOwnerRefused). The string pat:manage:any now grants nothing, asserted in PatManagementIT.

PAT admin area: PatAdminOperations (read/operate reserved/privileged), admin.service.PatAdminService over PatService and a new PatQueryRepository.findForAdministration (QueryDSL, keyset createdAt/id, status ACTIVE/EXPIRED/REVOKED mapped to revoked/expired booleans so the repository does not depend on the admin package), admin.web.PatAdminController under /admin/v1/pat/tokens, autoconfigure.PatAdminAutoConfiguration. Admin revoke uses RevocationReasons.REQUESTED and returns the token (200); admin issue skips the issue-time scope check exactly as issuance for another owner did before.

PAT credentials refused on /admin/v1/pat/** by registering the module's existing PatCredentialGuard for that pattern in PatAdminAutoConfiguration, independent of ludwig.admin.allow-personal-access-tokens; PatAdminIT runs with the flag true.

Grant blocks list exactly the areas each service has, read from the AdminGrants 'ungranted' startup log line, because a key naming an absent area fails startup. notification-service: jobs, outbox, identity, audit (all tiers NOTIFICATION_ADMIN, read tiers also NOTIFICATION_SUPPORT). crud-service-example: exports, fileactions, identity, jobs, outbox (all tiers CATALOG_ADMIN). Neither service exposed reconciliation or fileingest actuator endpoints, so nothing was removed there. YAML keys are bracketed because the ids contain a dot.

Both committed OpenAPI documents regenerated with scripts/api-docs.sh refresh; the diff adds the /admin/v1 paths, and existing operationIds are unchanged (paths only re-sorted). api-docs.sh check exits 0.

Manifest rebuilt (user-settings gained test-support-security).

failures: Task 1.2 attempt 1: ran security tests without -am, so it compiled against the stale audit-core in ~/.m2 (4-arg Actor) and failed to compile. Same process error as admin-authorization task 3.2; rerun with -am passed. Rule for this change: every module verification uses -am.

Task 3.2: one run of `mvn -pl :outbox-spring-boot-starter -am verify` failed every context in the module, old tests included, with PSQLException 'The connection attempt failed' / SocketTimeoutException from the Testcontainers Postgres. Test mistakes along the way, each fixed: @Primary capturing AuditSink collided with audit-core's primary composite (plain bean is collected by the composite); an unused import left by the package split.

12.1 verify, first run: PatDirectAuthenticationIT$FilterEnabled.revokedTokenStopsWorking ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException (the known last-used-tracker vs revoke race, already in admin-surface-follow-ups section 1). Rerun green, unchanged code.

Fixed at the source: IdentityProjectionAutoConfiguration is now @AutoConfiguration(before = {LudwigSecurityAutoConfiguration, MutualTlsAutoConfiguration}). The IT passes (8/8).

15.2 gate run 2 (reactor verify of all 26 gate modules): asyncapi-spring-boot-starter AsyncApiDocumentShapeIT 7 errors, NoClassDefFoundError ru/ludwigandreas/security/admin/AdminPage. Root cause: Springwolf's ComponentClassScanner reflects on every @Component class under ru.ludwigandreas, including OutboxAdminController whose methods return the security starter's AdminPage, absent in a service with outbox but no security starter - a real consumer-facing regression of this change. Fixed in asyncapi-spring-boot-starter: IntrospectableComponentClassScanner (skips classes whose methods cannot be resolved) registered by AsyncApiScannerAutoConfiguration before SpringwolfAutoConfiguration, whose own scanner is @ConditionalOnMissingBean. asyncapi verify: 51 + 7 green; reactor resumed from it.

open_questions: file-ingest-admin's '409 while running' scenario has no test: holding a pass mid-run from MockMvc needs a blocking object store in the test context. The code path (IngestPass.runOnce returning false -> FileIngestAdminException.alreadyRunning, audited as refused-by-state) mirrors the actuator's tested 'another instance holds the lock' branch. Candidate for ConcurrentReplicaIT's latch technique.

A cancelled file-action submission is recorded APPLIED with zero rows (FileActionService.stateFor ignores ApplyOutcome.stopped()); pre-existing, affects the requester cancel too, needs a lifecycle decision since CANCELLED is forbidden in FileActionState.
